title: Counting a Profile's Northbeam Renew Trade-In Year
content:
**Clause.** Trade-in activity under Northbeam Renew Trade-In is counted across the whole profile: the devices traded in the rolling year and the credit issued in the rolling year are compared with the figures of the Renew programme the new quote is written under. Where the device count is already at its limit no further quote is written until the window rolls on, and the customer is told the day the oldest device drops out of the count. Where the value cap is already reached the quote is still written but the credit is issued only up to whatever room the cap leaves, and the remainder is not carried into the next year. Devices on agreements that expired or were sent back do not count, because no credit was issued; recycling credits do count. A business profile is counted together across its named buyers, and a consumer profile only for itself.

**The two running figures.**

- *Devices traded in the rolling year.* The devices covered by the profile's trade-in agreements that stand credited, added up over the rolling twelve calendar months ending on the day the matter is handled.
- *Credit issued in the rolling year.* The trade-in credit issued on every agreement of the profile, added up over the rolling twelve calendar months ending on the day the matter is handled.

**What each ceiling does when it is reached.** The two behave differently, and the difference is the point of the clause:

| Ceiling reached | What happens to the quote | What happens to the credit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the devices traded in the rolling year is at the programme's limit | no further quote is written until the window rolls on, and the customer is told the day the oldest device drops out of the count | — |
| the credit issued in the rolling year is at the programme's value cap | the quote is still written | the credit is issued only up to the room the cap leaves, and the remainder is not carried into the next year |

**Points of judgement.**

- A device on an agreement that expired, or one that was sent back, is not in the count, the ground being that no credit was issued on it.
- A recycling credit is counted, being credit issued.
- Where the profile is a business profile, the count is taken across its named buyers together; a consumer profile is counted only for itself.
